title: Stream connection lifecycle: reclaim orphaned partial generations and reconcile client timeouts
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem summary: We still see customer-facing errors and resource waste when clients disconnect mid-stream (abrupt socket close, HTTP/2 RST_STREAM, or mobile backgrounding). These orphaned in-progress generations can keep GPU kernels or KV cache pinned, create stale partial outputs in our ephemeral stores, and cause metric skew (requests appear active longer than they are). Additionally, clients that time out and reconnect have inconsistent semantics across SDKs: some send explicit cancel signals, some simply close the connection. This inconsistency leads to partial-tool-call side effects and makes billing/trace continuity confusing.

Goal: Implement robust server-side detection and reclamation for abandoned streaming requests, add flow-control improvements (per-request pending-byte limits and window tokens), and expose compatibility fixes in SDKs so older clients are handled safely. The outcome should reduce leaked GPU/KV memory, shorten mean time-to-cleanup for orphaned streams, and provide predictable semantics for clients that time out or disconnect without a formal cancel handshake.
acceptance_criteria: Server immediately marks a stream as cancelled when it receives an explicit cancel signal (gRPC cancel, HTTP/2 RST_STREAM, WebSocket close).
Orphaned partial generations are reclaimed within 60s (hard TTL) with typical cleanup latency < 5s for common cases.
Metrics exist: orphaned_streams_count, orphan_cleanup_latency_p50/p95, leaked_kv_bytes, stream_active_duration (corrected for cancel).
SDKs (JS + Python) send cancel tokens on disconnect where supported, and fall back to sending an explicit 'abandon' event when the connection closes unexpectedly.
No customer-visible regressions: streaming latencies remain within ±5% in canary traffic; no increase in generation errors.
technical_notes: Server-side generation state: persist ephemeral metadata (generation_id, model_variant, kv_refs, pending_bytes) in an in-memory table keyed by request_id. This table is the unit of reclamation.

Flow-control: implement token-window per-stream (configurable default window 64KB). The runtime will block enqueuing more tokens if pending_bytes > 4MB. This prevents head-of-line resource exhaustion.

Cancellation signals to observe: 1) gRPC CANCEL / context.Canceled, 2) HTTP/2 RST_STREAM, 3) WebSocket CLOSE (1000 vs abnormal codes), 4) TCP connection close as last resort via socket EOF. For older clients that close without a protocol cancel, treat socket EOF as implicit abort.

Partial-generation preservation: short-lived soft checkpoint every N tokens (default N=32) written to ephemeral store to allow resume for clients that support continuation tokens. Soft checkpoints are stored for 120s by default, then evicted unless resumed.

KV cache cleanup: track kv_refs per generation; on cancel/cleanup, decrement reference counts and schedule background GC to free GPU/KV memory. Avoid synchronous large frees on hot paths; use batched async frees.

Compatibility layer: add an 'abandon' event that client SDKs can emit on connection close. Server treats 'abandon' like explicit cancel but records last-seen offset to help debugging. Older clients that cannot emit 'abandon' will still be covered by socket EOF detection.
Observability: trace events for stream lifecycle (created -> streaming -> cancelled/finished -> cleaned_up). Emit a span tag when cleanup took > 250ms.
tasks: Design: finalize lifecycle state machine and TTL parameters (Maya)
Runtime: implement request_state table + cancel handler (Ethan)
Runtime: add pending_bytes enforcement & token-window flow control (Ethan)
Client SDKs: JS & Python emit 'abandon' on close and expose isCancelled hooks (DevEx)
Testing: unit tests for cancel paths, chaos tests for abrupt disconnects, integration load test to reproduce leak and validate cleanup
Observability: dashboard & alerts for orphaned_streams_count and orphan_cleanup_latency
Docs & Runbook: update streaming runbook with steps to triage orphaned streams and emergency kill procedures
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Patel: Created ticket after reviewing customer incident where streaming sessions accrued 2.3GB of pinned KV over 48 hours. Attached initial waveform and heap samples to design doc.

2025-02-16 Ethan Chong: Prototype of request_state table complete. Observed that socket EOF detection differs between our HTTP/2 and WebSocket proxies; will add proxy-side fast-path to surface 'client_closed' event to runtime (see link to internal PR).

2025-02-18 Talia Grant (SRE): Ran chaos test with 10k simulated client disconnects. Without reclamation we leaked ~120MB/minute; prototype reclaim reduces to <3MB/minute. Next: add batched KV frees to avoid p99 latency spikes.
2025-02-21 DevEx Team: Drafted SDK change to add 'sendAbandonOnClose' opt-in flag. Default will remain off for backward compatibility; will enable behind feature flag during canary.

2025-02-24 Ethan Chong: Implemented server cancel hook, basic pending_bytes enforcement, and initial metrics. Pushed draft PR for review. Unit tests added; integration tests failing on one edge-case for resumed continuations (investigating).
